\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دیور} (devar)}{دیور (devar)}]{\ur{دیور} (devar) — a husband's younger brother}

\label{lesson:UR-C489-devar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a son-in-law, then the Urdu for to marry off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دیور}}
\textbf{\ur{دیور}} — \emph{devar} — \textquotedblleft{}a husband's younger brother\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میرا} \ur{دیور} \ur{کالج} \ur{میں} \ur{پڑھتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merā devar kālij meṅ paṛhtā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My husband's younger brother is at college.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دیور}} (\emph{devar}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{dēvara}, \textquotedblleft{}husband's younger brother\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6546).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{devar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{devar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{merā devar kālij meṅ paṛhtā hai.} — My husband's younger brother is at college.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a son-in-law, then the Urdu for to marry off, then say \emph{devar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{دیور} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A husband's younger brother\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نواسا} (navāsā)}{نواسا (navāsā)}]{\ur{نواسا} (navāsā) — a grandson (a daughter's son)}

\label{lesson:UR-C489-navasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a husband's sister, then the Urdu for a nephew (a sister's son).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نواسا}}
\textbf{\ur{نواسا}} — \emph{navāsā} — \textquotedblleft{}a grandson (a daughter's son)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
